release_notes: Media Experiment Ledger Studio 1.0.0-rc.5 completes the resource-aware scheduling milestone. Jobs now reserve a CPU slot or a provider/device-specific accelerator budget before process creation, with conservative input-size memory estimates, configurable safety reserves and visible queue reasons. Detection uses bounded persistent engine workers and reuses compatible ONNX Runtime sessions until idle eviction; pause, cancel and application shutdown terminate workers and release reservations. Accelerator and host out-of-memory failures are classified with actionable lower-resolution, lower-concurrency and CPU recovery guidance.
features: Provider/device-specific admission control replaces the fixed global concurrency limit
Configurable CPU concurrency, accelerator concurrency, declared memory budgets and safety reserves
Per-device overrides for DirectML, CUDA and CoreML resources
Conservative detection memory estimates derived from input dimensions and batch size
Explicit estimated_vram_mb override for advanced workloads
Queue stages and Hardware Runtime Center explain the exact blocking resource
Bounded persistent Detection workers keyed by model, provider, device and fallback policy
Compatible ONNX Runtime sessions are reused within warm workers
Configurable idle eviction closes workers and releases accelerator memory
Queued pause and cancel complete immediately without reserving resources
Running pause, cancel and application shutdown abort engine processes and release reservations
Accelerator and host out-of-memory classification includes actionable recovery guidance
Scheduler admission, safety reserve, memory estimation, OOM and persistent protocol tests
